candidates.description: Render a deterministic source brief for declared article-cluster IDs from the repository's existing asset-card corpus.
candidates.maintainer: Ignition repository maintainers; this field does not grant Owner or scientific authority.
good_for: Preparing a source-linked inventory of the members and declared status of a known article cluster.
Finding source and evidence fields already recorded in the repository's governed asset cards.
not_for: Determining whether a cluster's claims are true.
Producing a finished or publication-approved article.
Looking up clusters or sources outside the checked-out repository snapshot.
only_if: The requested cluster ID exists in ignition/analysis/corpus-relation/article_cluster_candidates.json.
The governed Knowledge card corpus and source parser are available in the same checkout.
counterindicated_when: The task requires live or freshly updated external sources.
The task asks for scientific adjudication, proof, or external evidence validation.
The cluster snapshot is stale for the user's requested time period.
side_effects: Writes only the JSON receipt to stdout; does not create or overwrite repository files.

estimated_cost.basis: No comparable timing, token, memory, or compute-cost profile has been established.

alternatives.reason: The registered operation provides source-bounded knowledge summaries but does not render this cluster-member brief contract.

candidates.fallback: If the cluster ID or source data is unavailable, stop and report the missing reference; read the canonical asset cards manually without substituting an inferred cluster.

negative_controls: Unknown cluster ID returns nonzero and emits no partial brief.
--stdout creates or overwrites no repository file.

router_conditions: Only include through an explicit experimental-tool allowlist for source-brief tasks.
Do not invoke after selection without the task's own user authorization and input.
candidates.claim_ceiling: A formatted projection of repository-local cluster metadata and asset-card fields only; no truth, proof, external evidence, article quality, acceptance, or publication status is inferred.

candidates.description: Select a sufficient set of registered operations for exact input and output requirements, optionally considering explicitly allowlisted experimental cards.
candidates.maintainer: Ignition repository maintainers; this field does not grant Owner or scientific authority.
good_for: Planning routes from explicit input types and required output types.
Showing when a task needs one operation, complementary operations, or remains uncovered.
Keeping experimental tools opt-in and returning an explicit incomplete result when no declared route covers a requirement.
not_for: Inferring the task contract from unstructured natural language.
Calling, dispatching, or executing selected operations.
Granting permissions, Owner approval, or scientific authority.
Claiming measured cost optimality or a globally minimal set.
only_if: The caller supplies exact input types, required outputs, allowed modes, and a nonblank Current reference string; the planner echoes that string without resolving it.
The operation registry and pinned experimental candidate-card source are present.
counterindicated_when: Task requirements cannot be expressed with the declared input/output types.
The caller needs actual tool execution or a scientific conclusion rather than a route proposal.
The current operation registry no longer matches the candidate-card source pin.
accepted_input_types: typed toolbox route profile on stdin

estimated_cost.basis: The selection run is local, but no calibrated latency, memory, or compute-cost comparison exists.

alternatives.reason: The existing single-operation lifecycle planner resolves one declared operation; this preview selects a typed set and still does not execute it.

candidates.fallback: If exact typed coverage is unavailable, return INCOMPLETE and use the existing single-operation planner or report the missing capability; never guess an operation from natural-language similarity.

negative_controls: Owner-deferred, historical, unsupported, and external-action operations are not selected.
Experimental tools remain excluded unless their IDs are explicitly allowlisted.
Unknown required outputs yield INCOMPLETE and do not cause dispatch.

candidates.description: Resolve an ordered batch of exact references against the checked-out Current canonical identity, alias, correction, claim, and legacy-mapping authorities; emit a source-hashed receipt to stdout.
candidates.maintainer: Ignition repository maintainers; this field does not grant Owner or scientific authority.
good_for: Resolving multiple exact IDs, canonical titles, registered aliases, and authority-backed identity corrections in one input-ordered batch.
Producing a reproducible receipt with SHA-256 references to the resolver and five Current authority snapshots.
Preserving ambiguous and unresolved references as explicit outcomes instead of dropping or guessing them.
not_for: Fuzzy, semantic, natural-language, web, or cross-repository identity search.
Changing identities, repairing source data, or writing results into the repository.
Establishing scientific truth, proof, external validity, or evidence quality.
only_if: The caller supplies a nonempty JSON object containing exactly one key, references, whose value is a nonempty array of nonblank strings.
All five Current authority files and the existing exact resolver are available in the same repository snapshot.
The caller accepts repository-snapshot resolution semantics and an output receipt on stdout.
counterindicated_when: The task requires fresh external sources, fuzzy matching, or resolution beyond the checked-out repository snapshot.
An ambiguous or unresolved result must be automatically selected or corrected.
The task asks for scientific adjudication, proof, or evidence validation.
accepted_input_types: JSON stdin object with an ordered nonempty array of exact reference strings
side_effects: Writes the result only to stdout; malformed input and unavailable authority are reported to stderr with nonzero status; no repository files are created or changed.

estimated_cost.basis: The resolver rebuilds exact lookup indexes for each reference; no comparable batch latency or memory benchmark has been established.

alternatives.reason: The Current operation exposes the single-reference resolver contract; this experimental CLI adds ordered multi-reference input and a batch receipt while reusing that resolver algorithm.

candidates.fallback: For one reference, use the existing foundation.resolve_current_asset operation or ignition/tools/foundation/resolve_current_canonical_asset.py --reference; if this batch tool is unavailable, process references individually and preserve each unresolved or ambiguous status.

negative_controls: Unknown, historical-path, and near-match references remain explicitly unresolved in input order.
Malformed batches, path traversal, and symlinked authorities fail closed without partial stdout output.
Running the CLI creates or changes no repository files.

router_conditions: Include only through an explicit experimental-tool allowlist for exact multi-reference repository identity resolution.
The route proposal does not execute the tool; the caller must separately authorize and supply the specific batch input.
Do not select when fuzzy matching, external freshness, scientific judgment, or automatic identity repair is required.
candidates.claim_ceiling: Repository-snapshot canonical identity and migration resolution only; ambiguous and unresolved rows remain explicit; no fuzzy identity, truth, proof, evidence upgrade, or external validity is inferred.
